result.rationale: The diff shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` in the public groups_controller.rb members action, with no upper bound on limit. Unlike the old code where caller-controlled limit applied only to automatic groups (default 200), the new code applies it to all groups, so any unauthenticated-permission caller can request arbitrarily large page sizes, forcing oversized DB queries and serialized payloads. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb lines 22-23 that `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any user-provided limit value without an upper bound. While there's a default of 50, an attacker could pass limit=1000000 to force the server to serialize an extremely large number of users, potentially causing memory exhaustion or timeout. This is a real security/DoS vulnerability - the code should cap the limit to a reasonable maximum value.
